setlist.title: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **It's All Over Now Baby Blue** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Jerry's voice and guitar sound crisp and clear throughout this Baby Blue; Calls this Baby Blue unrivaled, technically perfect, and the best recording of the song; regrets it was never released commercially [5][6][8]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): Singled out He's Gone, Playin' in the Band, and a tight, well-played Greatest Story as standouts; Calls this the best He's Gone ever, self-contained, with an impromptu Jerry blues solo after the doo-wop chorus [7][11]
- **Truckin'** (2 reviews): Jams run from Truckin' through The Other One into a brief spacey passage before Jerry eases into Baby Blue; Praises the Truckin' > The Other One > Baby Blue run, plus Weir's almost flawless Truckin' vocal [6][9]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Reviewer came for Cold Rain and Snow and enjoyed the solos [13]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Cumberland Blues has a cut in the soundboard; otherwise it might be the reviewer's favorite version [17]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Notes a pleasing variation in Bird Song, and strong versions of Greatest Story and Black Throated Wind [9]

## The recordings

- **gd72-09-26.sbd.unknown.156.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 185 min; rated 4.67/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is very nice; the mix is praised; Soundboard is deep and clean, with clear high guitars and slow vocals [9][13]
- **gd72-09-26.sbd.wier.19198.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound is clear and good [7]
- **gd1972-09-26.partial-sbd-patched.powell-ladner.25281.shnf**: soundboard; 3 songs; 41 min [5]
- **gd1972-09-26.sbd.unknown.sbexx.16755.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended all three Stanley Theatre nights and rated Thursday best, with Tuesday having superlative moments [8]
- Attended the three-night Stanley run; recalls this as the middle night [15]
- Would choose the 9/27 show last for a Dick's Pick release among the three Stanley nights [8]
- Recommended for fans of the Dick's Picks Stanley Theater release from the following night [11]
- Mentions the band's spring Academy of Music run, Roosevelt Stadium, and Dillon Stadium in Hartford that year [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-09-26.sbd.unknown.156.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: A version exists with an audience patch covering the Cumberland cut; Soundboard reel to unknown DAT generations, then digital noise reduction, three DAT generations, then a 48-41 conversion [1][17]
- **gd72-09-26.sbd.wier.19198.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1972-09-26.partial-sbd-patched.powell-ladner.25281.shnf**: transferred by Jim Powell and Chris Ladner; source: Splice upgrade - see info file for details [5]. Also: Partial soundboard patched with audience source; cassette to DAT transfer by J. Powell, DAT to SHN by C. Ladner [5]
- **gd1972-09-26.sbd.unknown.sbexx.16755.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Unknown; source: SBD > Master Reel [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by johnsdeadart.blogspot.com: [John's Custom Grateful Dead Album Cover Art](https://johnsdeadart.blogspot.com/2017/05/blog-post_90.html) [19]
- Poster by rocktourdatabase.com: [Grateful Dead | rocktourdatabase.com](https://rocktourdatabase.com/concerts/grateful-dead-996) [20]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Stanley Theatre - September 27, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/september-27-1972) [21]
